messages:
maria.g: hitting intermittent 401s when calling Redwood hosted API from a Next.js Edge API route (vercel edge runtime). Started after upgrading node-ts-sdk to 2.5.0, same code works from serverless. Anyone seen this? :thinking:

alex.k: can you paste a minimal repro and where this runs (browser vs edge function)? also which route on our API is failing?

maria.g: running in an Edge route (/app/api/generate/route.ts) with export const runtime = 'edge'. It's a server->server call from the edge function to our hosted API. The failing endpoint is /v1/chat/completions. Happens intermittently in prod, consistently in staging when keepalive is set on fetch. Code snippet:

```ts
// edge route snippet
export const runtime = 'edge'
const res = await fetch('https://api.redwood.example/v1/chat/completions', {
  method: 'POST',
  headers: {
    'Authorization': `Bearer ${token}`,
    'Content-Type': 'application/json'
  },
  credentials: 'include',
  keepalive: true, // toggle this and it reproduces
  body: JSON.stringify({ messages })
})
```

On keepalive:true the Edge route logs show a 401 from our backend. If I remove keepalive it succeeds every time. From a regular serverless function or node, keepalive:true doesn't cause issues.

alex.k: interesting. do you see any redirects? and can you capture the request/response headers for the failing attempt (edge logs)? Also can you try a curl from a remote host to simulate an OPTIONS preflight?

maria.g: I captured logs. When keepalive:true the first call returns 401. I also tried a curl that triggers a preflight (OPTIONS) and that returns 401 unless I explicitly include Access-Control-Allow-Headers on the API side. curl repro (simplified):

```bash
curl -i -X OPTIONS 'https://api.redwood.example/v1/chat/completions' \n  -H 'Origin: https://myapp.vercel.app' \n  -H 'Access-Control-Request-Method: POST' \n  -H 'Access-Control-Request-Headers: authorization,content-type'
```

Server returns 401 unless I add a permissive CORS rule. BUT the weird part is that our hosted API already allowed Authorization in ACAH and it works for normal requests. The pattern: Edge + keepalive -> 401. Edge without keepalive -> OK.

ingrid.r: :eyes: thanks for the repro. This smells like a known bug in the edge runtime's underlying fetch (undici/edge-proxy) where connection reuse + keepalive can cause the Authorization header to be dropped on pooled sockets or across redirects. Cloud/edge proxies sometimes strip headers when keep-alive semantics interact with their front proxy.

ingrid.r: immediate workaround: don't set keepalive in Edge routes, or explicitly set keepalive: false. You can also move the call to a serverless (node) function if you need keepalive. Example quick fix:

```ts
// workaround for now
const res = await fetch(url, { method:'POST', headers, keepalive:false, body })
```

ingrid.r: longer term: we'll triage whether the SDK (node-ts-sdk) should avoid enabling keepalive by default when it detects the edge runtime, or add a flag to opt out. I'm going to open an internal issue to track (ENG-RUNTIME-###).

maria.g: removing keepalive fixed staging immediately. Confirmed prod rollback looks good. Thanks.

alex.k: can you add the staging request IDs to the issue and paste any edge logs? also tagging eng-runtime to evaluate changing SDK defaults. :thumbsup:

support-bot: escalation created: #eng-runtime / ENG-RUNTIME-402 — edge keepalive drops auth header on Vercel edge runtime. Participants: maria.g, alex.k, ingrid.r.

maria.g: one more Q — should we push a patch to our codebase to detect runtime === 'edge' and avoid keepalive, or rely on the SDK change?

ingrid.r: short term add the guard in your app to be safe. medium term SDK will avoid setting keepalive for edge bundles and we'll add a release note. I'll update ENG-RUNTIME-402 with recommended patterns and a link to a follow-up PR.

maria.g: awesome, thanks all. saved my weekend :) :rocket:
